To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the transportation model is an efficient method for generating a raster map when the area weights are computed using the calibration estimator.
the methods based on a transportation problem can be used for raster map generation in forest inventory, if they are followed by local averaging and the area size is small enough.
the area weights computed with the calibration estimator can be used for raster map generation using the transportation model.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of the raster map generation methods for a forest resource inventory.
the development of methods for raster map generation and with their comparison to the RSP method.
developing a method for generating raster maps of forest resources.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the method based on solving the transportaion problem does not perform as well as the reference method, the RSP, in the test area.
the methods of this thesis do not provide a solution for the problem of generating a raster map presentation from a sample plot inventory.
the method based on solving the transport problem is a good alternative to the nearest neighbour method, if the pixel level error is not a problem.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the transportation approach has not yet reached the level of usability for practical applications.
the methods presented in this thesis can be used for generating raster maps of forest resources, but they are not ready to be applied for large areas, such as municipalities.

, in the present study we have shown that the transportation model can be used to solve the area weight allocation problem in raster map generation, and that the method is promising for further development.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the methods based on calibration estimation can be used as an alternative method of area weight calculation, when the area is small enough to be processed pixel by pixel, and the area weight is needed for raster map generation.
the transportation model is a feasible approach for the raster map generation, but further development is needed.
the methods based on calibration estimation are not yet usable for the raster map generation, but the transportation model approach can be a promising tool for this purpose.
